protections: setUrl() trims the string and rejects URLs whose lower-cased form starts with file://, file:/, file:\ or file:\\ before storing them (src/Browsershot.php:258-274).
setHtml() rejects any HTML string containing the literal substrings file:// or file:/ before storing it (src/Browsershot.php:296-308).

setHtmlFromFilePath() checks only that the path exists, then builds a file:// URL from it (src/Browsershot.php:276-287); there is no trust or allow-list check, so this guard protects only against missing files.
The Node bridge reads a URL-derived filesystem path with fs.readFileSync whenever options.contentUrl is set, with no protocol or path validation (bin/browser.cjs:116-123, 293).
Opt-in request interception can abort requests by URL substring or hostname (bin/browser.cjs:177-192; src/Browsershot.php:471-479); it is not a default protection and has no file-scheme rule.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Browsershot::url() is the documented factory and the only in-tree caller of setUrl (src/Browsershot.php:71-74); the constructor's $url argument is treated as internal, so a direct new Browsershot($visitorUrl) is not expected to be attacker-reachable.

The guard rejects the literal file:// and file:/ in the HTML, and the HTML in this route contains no URL scheme at all: it is ordinary markup whose root-relative or dot-dot reference resolves against the page's own file:// base, so the check looks complete.

file:/ and file:// are already refused and the URL setter additionally lists the backslash forms (src/Browsershot.php:262); backslashes read as a Windows spelling of the same separator that the other guard already handles.

htmlFromFilePath() is a documented feature (README.md:34-38, tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17) whose whole purpose is to render a caller-chosen local HTML file, and the path is supplied by the developer rather than the visitor.

setContentUrl() only stores contentUrl when html() was used (src/Browsershot.php:989), and in that case request.url is the library's own temp file, so the fs.readFileSync looks like it can only ever read that temp file.

masking: T2 is masked by the literal check: because the guard visibly rejects file:// in HTML (src/Browsershot.php:298), the resolved-path route created by the library's own file:// base (src/Browsershot.php:1028-1030) is easy to overlook as already covered.

T5 is masked by T1/T2: while file:// navigation is reachable at all, the contentUrl read in the bridge is redundant; once every file:// navigation is blocked, the fs.readFileSync branch (bin/browser.cjs:121) becomes the surviving local-read path.

conflicts.what: Changing how setHtml() HTML is loaded (a non-file origin, or aborting file:// requests in the bridge) also removes the local-file base that htmlFromFilePath() relies on to render a local HTML file together with its relative assets (src/Browsershot.php:283 vs 1030; tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17).

Fixing T2 by serving setHtml() content from a data:/about:blank origin changes the command URL that the contentUrl feature and tests/BrowsershotTest.php:945-970 expect to be a file:// temp path (src/Browsershot.php:1028-1030, 1208).

A blanket rule that every URL assignment must pass the setUrl() file check closes the constructor route but also closes htmlFromFilePath() (src/Browsershot.php:283), which must keep producing a file:// URL.

fairness_risks: htmlFromFilePath() is documented (README.md:34-38) and tested (tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17); any rule that forbids local file rendering refuses a legitimate, documented use.

setContentUrl() is documented (docs/miscellaneous-options/using-url-for-html-content.md:6-12) and tests/BrowsershotTest.php:945-970 asserts the command URL is file://; a rule forbidding file:// in the bridge breaks relative-path resolution.

Local HTML that references local images or styles by root-relative or dot-dot paths is legitimate when rendering a file supplied through htmlFromFilePath(); a rule that refuses such markup in every HTML input refuses that use.

The existing setHtml() rule already refuses any HTML containing the literal text file:// even where it is only displayed or linked (src/Browsershot.php:298); tightening the same rule must not add false positives on ordinary documentation text.

setOption() is documented as accepting any option (docs/miscellaneous-options/setting-an-arbirary-option.md:6-12); guarding internal options such as contentUrl must not break that documented escape hatch.

design.why: T1, T2 (with T3 as a second surface of the same guard) and T5 sit at three unrelated fix sites - the constructor (src/Browsershot.php:86-88), the HTML origin versus the HTML string guard (src/Browsershot.php:298 vs 1028-1030) and the bridge's contentUrl read (bin/browser.cjs:121) - so no single change closes more than one group, and each has a different reason to dismiss: 'the factory is the documented API', 'the HTML contains no URL scheme', and 'contentUrl only runs with html'. The mix pairs deepseek-type route-absent-plus-dismiss traps (T1, T5) with a mimo-type how-type mechanism (T2), and the documented htmlFromFilePath()/setContentUrl() behaviour is a real over-hardening trap for MiMo. T4 is the strongest deepseek-type trap (M4 with a documented-feature excuse) but is excluded from the default design because its only clean fix contradicts README.md:34-38 and tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17; it should be added only if the task scopes htmlFromFilePath() to untrusted paths explicitly. T3 is listed with T2 because one robust guard at the navigation/request layer (or a non-file document origin) closes both, so it is not counted as an independent group.

unverified: The exact B route closed by the 2025-02-05 fix e32739745068 cannot be determined from the pinned tree. T2 is the reading most consistent with 'bypass of the fix' that is not a pure spelling/encoding variant, but this is unconfirmed.

headerHtml()/footerHtml() accept arbitrary HTML with no file:// check (src/Browsershot.php:352-360); whether Chromium's print header/footer renderer loads file:// subresources - and therefore whether this is a real local-read sink or the B route - could not be verified.

Chromium normalises backslash separators for the file: scheme, so HTML such as 'file:' followed by three backslashes and a path should resolve to a file URL and evade src/Browsershot.php:298; not verified against a browser here.

A bare file: scheme without slashes (for example setUrl('file:etc/passwd'), or HTML 'file:../../etc/passwd') passes both guards (src/Browsershot.php:262, 298); whether it resolves to a local path was not verified, and it is arguably a protocol variant and therefore not recordable as a trap.
view-source:file:///... passes the setUrl prefix check (src/Browsershot.php:262-268); whether page.goto renders the local file source was not verified, and it is arguably a protocol variant.
Leading form-feed or other C0 whitespace is not removed by PHP trim() (src/Browsershot.php:260) but is stripped by the WHATWG URL parser; not verified in this Chromium build.

No browser or shell was available in this session; all URL-resolution and file-loading claims rest on the WHATWG URL parser rules and Chromium's default file-origin subresource loading, not on a run of the pinned code.
